- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mendeley is described as a popular, free reference manager with a large academic community that allows organizing papers, annotating PDFs, and collaborating with others.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Zotero is described as a free, open-source citation manager that is highly customizable and integrates with Microsoft Word, Google Docs, and LibreOffice.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] EndNote is described as a commercial citation manager widely used in academia, offering advanced features like automatic citation formatting and collaboration tools.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cite This For Me is a web-based citation tool that allows creating and organizing citations in various styles and includes a plagiarism checker and grammar editor.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Papers is described as a commercial reference manager designed for researchers, offering a clean interface and collaboration features.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Citavi is described as a comprehensive research management tool that includes citation management, note-taking, and task management features.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] ReadCube is described as a free reference manager that allows organizing papers, annotating PDFs, and discovering new research.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant advised the user to explore the features and user interfaces of each tool to determine which one works best for them.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided tips for ensuring comprehensive coverage of literature in the user's field, including starting with a broad search, using multiple databases, searching beyond journals, citation tracking, analyzing citation networks, consulting with experts, using systematic review methods, maintaining a "parked" list, regularly updating searches, and using literature mapping tools.
